requirements.heading: Additional parameters for RCPT and MAIL commands
requirements.text: Therefore, while parentheses MAY appear within an emstp-value, they are not recognized as comment delimiters.

requirements.heading: Additional parameters for RCPT and MAIL commands
requirements.text: + Any ASCII CHAR between "!" and "~" inclusive, except for "+" and "=", MAY be encoded as itself.

requirements.heading: Additional parameters for RCPT and MAIL commands
requirements.text: (A CHAR in this range MAY instead be encoded as a "hexchar", at the implementor's discretion.)

requirements.heading: The NOTIFY parameter of the ESMTP RCPT command
requirements.text: If the NOTIFY esmtp-keyword is used, it MUST have an associated esmtp-value, formatted according to the following rules, using the ABNF of RFC 822:

requirements.heading: The NOTIFY parameter of the ESMTP RCPT command
requirements.text: Multiple notify-list-elements, separated by commas, MAY appear in a NOTIFY parameter; however, the NEVER keyword MUST appear by itself.

requirements.heading: The ORCPT parameter to the ESMTP RCPT command
requirements.text: If the ORCPT esmtp-keyword is used, it MUST have an associated esmtp-value, which consists of the original recipient address, encoded according to the rules below.

requirements.heading: The ORCPT parameter to the ESMTP RCPT command
requirements.text: The "addr-type" portion MUST be an IANA-registered electronic mail address-type (as defined in [3]), while the "xtext" portion contains an encoded representation of the original recipient address using the rules in section 5 of this document.

requirements.heading: The ORCPT parameter to the ESMTP RCPT command
requirements.text: The entire ORCPT parameter MAY be up to 500 characters in length.

requirements.heading: The ORCPT parameter to the ESMTP RCPT command
requirements.text: When initially submitting a message via SMTP, if the ORCPT parameter is used, it MUST contain the same address as the RCPT TO address (unlike the RCPT TO address, the ORCPT parameter will be encoded as xtext).

requirements.heading: The ORCPT parameter to the ESMTP RCPT command
requirements.text: Likewise, when a mailing list submits a message via SMTP to be distributed to the list subscribers, if ORCPT is used, the ORCPT parameter MUST match the new RCPT TO address of each recipient, not the address specified by the original sender of the message.)

requirements.heading: The ORCPT parameter to the ESMTP RCPT command
requirements.text: Due to limitations in the Delivery Status Notification format, the value of the original recipient address prior to encoding as "xtext" MUST consist entirely of printable (graphic and white space) characters from the US-ASCII [4] repertoire.

requirements.heading: The ORCPT parameter to the ESMTP RCPT command
requirements.text: If an addr-type is defined for addresses which use characters outside of this repertoire, the specification for that addr-type MUST define the means of encoding those addresses in printable US-ASCII characters when are then encoded as xtext.

requirements.heading: The RET parameter of the ESMTP MAIL command
requirements.text: If the RET esmtp-keyword is used, it MUST have an associated esmtp-value, which is one of the following keywords:

requirements.heading: The RET parameter of the ESMTP MAIL command
requirements.text: If no RET parameter is supplied, the MTA MAY return either the headers of the message or the entire message for any DSN containing indication of failed deliveries.

requirements.heading: The ENVID parameter to the ESMTP MAIL command
requirements.text: The ENVID esmtp-keyword MUST have an associated esmtp-value.

requirements.heading: The ENVID parameter to the ESMTP MAIL command
requirements.text: The ENVID parameter MAY be up to 100 characters in length.

requirements.heading: The ENVID parameter to the ESMTP MAIL command
requirements.text: Due to limitations in the Delivery Status Notification format, the value of the ENVID parameter prior to encoding as "xtext" MUST consist entirely of printable (graphic and white space) characters from the US-ASCII [4] repertoire.

requirements.heading: Restrictions on the use of Delivery Status Notification parameters
requirements.text: The RET and ENVID parameters MUST NOT appear more than once each in any single MAIL command.

requirements.heading: Restrictions on the use of Delivery Status Notification parameters
requirements.text: If more than one of either of these parameters appears in a MAIL command, the ESMTP server SHOULD respond with "501 syntax error in parameters or arguments".

requirements.heading: Restrictions on the use of Delivery Status Notification parameters
requirements.text: The NOTIFY and ORCPT parameters MUST NOT appear more than once in any RCPT command.

requirements.heading: Restrictions on the use of Delivery Status Notification parameters
requirements.text: If more than one of either of these parameters appears in a RCPT command, the ESMTP server SHOULD respond with "501 syntax error in parameters or arguments".

requirements.heading: Conformance requirements
requirements.text: An MTA which, when acting as an SMTP server, issues the DSN keyword in response to the EHLO command, MUST obey the rules below for a "conforming SMTP client" when acting as a client, and a "conforming SMTP server" when acting as a server.

requirements.heading: SMTP protocol interactions
requirements.text: (a) If an SMTP client issues a MAIL command containing a valid ENVID parameter and associated esmtp-value and/or a valid RET parameter and associated esmtp-value, a conforming SMTP server MUST return the same reply-code as it would to the same MAIL command without the ENVID and/or RET parameters.

requirements.heading: SMTP protocol interactions
requirements.text: A conforming SMTP server MUST NOT refuse a MAIL command based on the absence or presence of valid ENVID or RET parameters, or on their associated esmtp-values.

requirements.heading: SMTP protocol interactions
requirements.text: However, if the associated esmtp-value is not valid (i.e., contains illegal characters), or if there is more than one ENVID or RET parameter in a particular MAIL command, the server MUST issue the reply-code 501 with an appropriate message (e.g., "syntax error in parameter").

requirements.heading: SMTP protocol interactions
requirements.text: (b) If an SMTP client issues a RCPT command containing any valid NOTIFY and/or ORCPT parameters, a conforming SMTP server MUST return the same response as it would to the same RCPT command without those NOTIFY and/or ORCPT parameters.

requirements.heading: SMTP protocol interactions
requirements.text: A conforming SMTP server MUST NOT refuse a RCPT command based on the presence or absence of any of these parameters.

requirements.heading: SMTP protocol interactions
requirements.text: However, if any of the associated esmtp-values are not valid, or if there is more than one of any of these parameters in a particular RCPT command, the server SHOULD issue the response "501 syntax error in parameter".

requirements.heading: Handling of messages received via SMTP
requirements.text: NOTE: A DSN MUST NOT be returned to the sender for any message for which the return address from the SMTP MAIL command was NULL ("<>"), even if the sender's address is available from other sources (e.g., the message header).

requirements.heading: Handling of messages received via SMTP
requirements.text: However, the MTA which would otherwise issue a DSN SHOULD inform the local postmaster of delivery failures through some appropriate mechanism that will not itself result in the generation of DSNs.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to other conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: (a) Any ENVID parameter included in the MAIL command when a message was received, MUST also appear on the MAIL command with which the message is relayed, with the same associated esmtp-value.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to other conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: If no ENVID parameter was included in the MAIL command when the message was received, the ENVID parameter MUST NOT be supplied when the message is relayed.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to other conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: (b) Any RET parameter included in the MAIL command when a message was received, MUST also appear on the MAIL command with which the message is relayed, with the same associated esmtp-value.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to other conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: If no RET parameter was included in the MAIL command when the message was received, the RET parameter MUST NOT supplied when the message is relayed.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to other conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: (c) If the NOTIFY parameter was supplied for a recipient when the message was received, the RCPT command issued when the message is relayed MUST also contain the NOTIFY parameter along with its associated esmtp-value.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to other conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: If the NOTIFY parameter was not supplied for a recipient when the message was received, the NOTIFY parameter MUST NOT be supplied for that recipient when the message is relayed.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to other conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: (d) If any ORCPT parameter was present in the RCPT command for a recipient when the message was received, an ORCPT parameter with the identical original-recipient-address MUST appear in the RCPT command issued for that recipient when relaying the message.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to other conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: (For example, the MTA therefore MUST NOT change the case of any alphabetic characters in an ORCPT parameter.)

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to other conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: If no ORCPT parameter was present in the RCPT command when the message was received, an ORCPT parameter MAY be added to the RCPT command when the message is relayed.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to other conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: If an ORCPT parameter is added by the relaying MTA, it MUST contain the recipient address from the RCPT command used when the message was received by that MTA.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to non-conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: (a) ENVID, NOTIFY, RET, or ORCPT parameters MUST NOT be issued when relaying the message.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to non-conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: (b) If the NOTIFY parameter was supplied for a recipient, with an esmtp-value containing the keyword SUCCESS, and the SMTP server returns a success (2xx) reply-code in response to the RCPT command, the client MUST issue a "relayed" DSN for that recipient.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to non-conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: (c) If the NOTIFY parameter was supplied for a recipient with an esmtp-value containing the keyword FAILURE, and the SMTP server returns a permanent failure (5xx) reply-code in response to the RCPT command, the client MUST issue a "failed" DSN for that recipient.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to non-conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: (d) If the NOTIFY parameter was supplied for a recipient with an esmtp-value of NEVER, the client MUST NOT issue a DSN for that recipient, regardless of the reply-code returned by the SMTP server.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to non-conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: However, if the server returned a failure (5xx) reply-code, the client MAY inform the local postmaster of the delivery failure via an appropriate mechanism that will not itself result in the generation of DSNs.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to non-conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: When attempting to relay a message to an SMTP server that does not support this extension, and if NOTIFY=NEVER was specified for some recipients of that message, a conforming SMTP client MAY relay the message for those recipients in a separate SMTP transaction, using an empty reverse-path in the MAIL command.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to non-conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: (e) If a NOTIFY parameter was not supplied for a recipient, and the SMTP server returns a success (2xx) reply-code in response to a RCPT command, the client MUST NOT issue any DSN for that recipient.

requirements.heading: Relay of messages to non-conforming SMTP servers
requirements.text: (f) If a NOTIFY parameter was not supplied for a recipient, and the SMTP server returns a permanent failure (5xx) reply-code in response to a RCPT command, the client MUST issue a "failed" DSN for that recipient.

requirements.heading: Local delivery of messages
requirements.text: (a) If the NOTIFY parameter was supplied for that recipient, with an esmtp-value containing the SUCCESS keyword, the MTA MUST issue a "delivered" DSN for that recipient.

requirements.heading: Local delivery of messages
requirements.text: (b) If the NOTIFY parameter was supplied for that recipient which did not contain the SUCCESS keyword, the MTA MUST NOT issue a DSN for that recipient.

requirements.heading: Local delivery of messages
requirements.text: (c) If the NOTIFY parameter was not supplied for that recipient, the MTA MUST NOT issue a DSN.

requirements.heading: Gatewaying a message into a foreign environment
requirements.text: notification thus issued will be translated into a DSN and delivered to the original sender, then the MTA SHOULD gateway the message into the foreign environment, requesting notification under the desired conditions, without itself issuing a DSN.

requirements.heading: Gatewaying a message into a foreign environment
requirements.text: (b) If a NOTIFY parameter was supplied with the SUCCESS keyword, but the destination environment cannot return an appropriate notification on successful delivery, the MTA SHOULD issue a "relayed" DSN for that recipient.

requirements.heading: Gatewaying a message into a foreign environment
requirements.text: (c) If a NOTIFY parameter was supplied with an esmtp-keyword of NEVER, a DSN MUST NOT be issued.

requirements.heading: Gatewaying a message into a foreign environment
requirements.text: If possible, the MTA SHOULD direct the destination environment to not issue delivery notifications for that recipient.

requirements.heading: Gatewaying a message into a foreign environment
requirements.text: (d) If the NOTIFY parameter was not supplied for a particular recipient, a DSN SHOULD NOT be issued by the gateway.

requirements.heading: Gatewaying a message into a foreign environment
requirements.text: The gateway SHOULD attempt to ensure that appropriate notification will be provided by the foreign mail environment if eventual delivery failure occurs, and that no notification will be issued on successful delivery.

requirements.heading: Gatewaying a message into a foreign environment
requirements.text: (e) When gatewaying a message into a foreign environment, the return-of-content conditions specified by any RET parameter are nonbinding; however, the MTA SHOULD attempt to honor the request using whatever mechanisms exist in the foreign environment.

requirements.heading: Delays in delivery
requirements.text: If a conforming MTA receives a message via the SMTP protocol, and is unable to deliver or relay the message to one or more recipients for an extended length of time (to be determined by the MTA), it MAY issue a "delayed" DSN for those recipients, subject to the following conditions:

requirements.heading: Delays in delivery
requirements.text: (a) If the NOTIFY parameter was supplied for a recipient and its value included the DELAY keyword, a "delayed" DSN MAY be issued.

requirements.heading: Delays in delivery
requirements.text: (b) If the NOTIFY parameter was not supplied for a recipient, a "delayed" DSN MAY be issued.

requirements.heading: Delays in delivery
requirements.text: (c) If the NOTIFY parameter was supplied which did not contain the DELAY keyword, a "delayed" DSN MUST NOT be issued.

requirements.heading: Failure of a conforming MTA to deliver a message
requirements.text: (a) If a NOTIFY parameter was supplied for the recipient with an esmtp-keyword containing the value FAILURE, a "failed" DSN MUST be issued by the MTA.

requirements.heading: Failure of a conforming MTA to deliver a message
requirements.text: (b) If a NOTIFY parameter was supplied for the recipient which did not contain the value FAILURE, a DSN MUST NOT be issued for that recipient.

requirements.heading: Failure of a conforming MTA to deliver a message
requirements.text: However, the MTA MAY inform the local postmaster of the delivery failure via some appropriate mechanism which does not itself result in the generation of DSNs.

requirements.heading: Failure of a conforming MTA to deliver a message
requirements.text: (c) If no NOTIFY parameter was supplied for the recipient, a "failed" DSN MUST be issued.

requirements.heading: Failure of a conforming MTA to deliver a message
requirements.text: If a DSN is issued for such a recipient, the Action value MUST be "failed".

requirements.heading: Forwarding, aliases, and mailing lists
requirements.text: If the NOTIFY parameter for the list submission address contained the SUCCESS keyword, a "delivered" DSN MUST be returned to the sender of the original message.

requirements.heading: Forwarding, aliases, and mailing lists
requirements.text: However, even if a "delivered" DSN was issued by the MTA, a mailing list which rejects a message submission MAY notify the sender that the message was rejected using an ordinary message instead of a DSN.

requirements.heading: Forwarding, aliases, and mailing lists
requirements.text: This address MAY be that of a process that recognizes DSNs and processes them automatically, but it MUST forward unrecognized messages to the human responsible for the list.

requirements.heading: Forwarding, aliases, and mailing lists
requirements.text: (b) The ENVID, NOTIFY, RET, and ORCPT parameters which accompany the redistributed message MUST NOT be derived from those of the original message.

requirements.heading: Forwarding, aliases, and mailing lists
requirements.text: (c) The NOTIFY and RET parameters MAY be specified by the local postmaster or the list administrator.

requirements.heading: Forwarding, aliases, and mailing lists
requirements.text: If ORCPT parameters are supplied during redistribution to the list subscribers, they SHOULD contain the addresses of the list subscribers in the format used by the mailing list.

requirements.heading: Forwarding, aliases, and mailing lists
requirements.text: Under normal circumstances, when a message arrives for an "alias" which has a single forwarding address, a DSN SHOULD NOT be issued.

requirements.heading: Forwarding, aliases, and mailing lists
requirements.text: Any ENVID, NOTIFY, RET, or ORCPT parameters SHOULD be propagated with the message as it is redistributed to the forwarding address.

requirements.heading: DSNs describing delivery to multiple recipients
requirements.text: If a DSN is issued for some recipients in an SMTP transaction and not for others according to the rules above, the DSN SHOULD NOT contain information for recipients for whom DSNs would not otherwise have been issued.

requirements.heading: Handling of messages from other sources
requirements.text: However, if such requests are transmitted within the message itself (for example in the message headers), the requests MUST be removed from the message before it is transmitted via SMTP.

requirements.heading: Handling of messages from other sources
requirements.text: For messages gatewayed from non-SMTP sources and further relayed by SMTP, the gateway SHOULD, using the SMTP extensions described here, attempt to provide the delivery reporting conditions expected by the source mail environment.

requirements.heading: Handling of messages from other sources
requirements.text: If appropriate, any DSNs returned to the source environment SHOULD be translated into the format expected in that environment.

requirements.heading: Implementation limits
requirements.text: A conforming MTA MUST accept ESMTP parameters of at least the following sizes:

requirements.heading: Implementation limits
requirements.text: However, user agents which use SMTP as a message submission protocol SHOULD NOT generate ENVID parameters which are longer than 38 characters in length.

requirements.heading: Implementation limits
requirements.text: A conforming MTA MUST be able to accept SMTP command-lines which are at least 1036 characters long (530 characters for the ORCPT and NOTIFY parameters of the RCPT command, in addition to the 512

requirements.heading: Implementation limits
requirements.text: If other SMTP extensions are supported by the MTA, the MTA MUST be able to accept a command-line large enough for each SMTP command and any combination of ESMTP parameters which may be used with that command.

requirements.heading: SMTP Envelope to be used with Delivery Status Notifications
requirements.text: The DSN sender address (in the SMTP MAIL command) MUST be a null reverse-path ("<>"), as required by section 5.3.3 of [11].

requirements.heading: SMTP Envelope to be used with Delivery Status Notifications
requirements.text: When transmitting a DSN via SMTP, the RET parameter MUST NOT be used.

requirements.heading: SMTP Envelope to be used with Delivery Status Notifications
requirements.text: The NOTIFY parameter MAY be used, but its value MUST be NEVER.

requirements.heading: SMTP Envelope to be used with Delivery Status Notifications
requirements.text: The ENVID parameter (with a newly generated envelope-id) and/or ORCPT parameter MAY be used.

requirements.heading: Contents of the DSN
requirements.text: When the value of the RET parameter is FULL, the full message SHOULD be returned for any DSN which conveys notification of delivery failure.

requirements.heading: Contents of the DSN
requirements.text: (However, if the length of the message is greater than some implementation-specified length, the MTA MAY return only the headers even if the RET parameter specified FULL.) If a DSN contains no notifications of delivery failure, the MTA SHOULD return only the headers.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: (a) if an ENVID parameter was present on the MAIL command, an Original-Envelope-ID field MUST be supplied, and the value associated with the ENVID parameter must appear in that field.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: If the message was received via SMTP with no ENVID parameter, the Original-Envelope-ID field MUST NOT be supplied.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: (b) The Reporting-MTA field MUST be supplied.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: If Reporting MTA can determine its fully-qualified Internet domain name, the MTA- name-type subfield MUST be "dns", and the field MUST contain the fully-qualified domain name of the Reporting MTA.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: If the fully-qualified Internet domain name of the Reporting MTA is not known (for example, for an SMTP server which is not directly connected to the Internet), the Reporting-MTA field may contain any string identifying the MTA, however, in this case the MTA- name-type subfield MUST NOT be "dns".

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: (c) Other per-message fields as defined in [3] MAY be supplied as appropriate.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: (d) If the ORCPT parameter was provided for this recipient, the Original-Recipient field MUST be supplied, with its value taken from the ORCPT parameter.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: If no ORCPT parameter was provided for this recipient, the Original-Recipient field MUST NOT appear.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: (e) The Final-Recipient field MUST be supplied.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: It MUST contain the recipient address from the message envelope.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: (f) The Action field MUST be supplied.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: (g) The Status field MUST be supplied, using a status-code from [6].

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: If there is no specific code which suitably describes a delivery failure, either 4.0.0 (temporary failure), or 5.0.0 (permanent failure) MUST be used.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: (h) For DSNs resulting from attempts to relay a message to one or more recipients via SMTP, the Remote-MTA field MUST be supplied for each of those recipients.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: (i) For DSNs resulting from attempts to relay a message to one or more recipients via SMTP, the Diagnostic-Code MUST be supplied for each of those recipients.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: (j) For DSNs resulting from attempts to relay a message to one or more recipients via SMTP, an SMTP-Remote-Recipient extension field MAY be supplied for each recipient, which contains the address of that recipient which was presented to the remote SMTP server.

requirements.heading: Message/delivery-status fields
requirements.text: (k) Other per-recipient fields defined in [3] MAY appear, as appropriate.

requirements.heading: "rfc822" address-type
requirements.text: However, an MTA MUST NOT modify an address obtained from the message envelope to force it to conform to syntax rules.

requirements.heading: "smtp" diagnostic-type
requirements.text: For a single-line SMTP reply to an SMTP command, the diagnostic-code SHOULD be an exact transcription of the reply.

requirements.heading: "dns" MTA-name-type
requirements.text: MTA names of type "dns" SHOULD be valid Internet domain names.
